title: The CCP prepares for the Fifth Plenum, with Alexander Davey
gist: MERICS analyst Alexander Davey discusses the CCP's preparation for the Fifth Plenum ahead of the 21st National Congress, with Beijing prioritizing social and political stability and planning trillions of dollars in spending on 'the six networks' to offset weak domestic demand and stalled manufacturing investment.

insights.claim: Ahead of the 21st National Congress of the CCP next year, Beijing is doubling down on social and political stability.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Expect stability and party discipline to dominate policy choices into the Congress; watch Fifth Plenum signals.

insights.claim: Recent Politburo meetings have focused on strict governance of the party and on resolving problems facing 'party building' in preparation for the Fifth Plenum.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Signals inward political focus ahead of the plenum.

insights.claim: State Council Executive meeting readouts admit 'weakness in economic performance' and that insufficient domestic demand remains prominent.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Official acknowledgement of weak demand makes further support measures more likely.

insights.claim: To compensate for weak demand and stalled manufacturing investment, China plans to spend trillions of dollars on 'the six networks': water and pipeline, electricity, computing, communications, and logistics systems.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Infrastructure-led stimulus favors grid, computing, communications and logistics build-out beneficiaries; track announcements.
